chapter_theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 17 of 21): the household, wealth and kin left at the burning ground or seized at Death's coming, courtesans who take money, and pleas for the name and feet at the last hour, beside songs of inner yoga, of Siva-knowledge as a bride, of experience over scripture and sect, and of the threefold Tamil.
structure_note: Songs in order of their first letter (க, கி, கு, கோ, ச, சா, சி, சீ, சூ, செ, த). Household and wealth: 1235, 1238, 1239, 1245; Death: 1236, 1243, 1244; courtesans: 1233, 1237, 1242, 1243; the inner way: 1240, 1241, 1242, 1246. Five praises (1232, 1236, 1237, 1245 and, less clearly, 1233) have Murugan instruct Siva or call him guru to Siva.

1232.reading: The poet asks whether a day will come when, crossing the sea of birth with its deceitful fish and sharks in the boat of true speech, he will lay many flowers (kuravu, vetchi, mullai, utpalam, kadamba, vilvam and others) on Murugan and recite his words. The praise calls Murugan the one who spoke love to Valli born of the deer, guru to the lord whose limit Brahma and Vishnu could not see, and, with wordplay on தெய்வயானை, younger brother of the divine elephant, lord of the white elephant and dear to Devayanai.
1232.nuance: The plea is for flower worship and recitation (உனது சொல்லை ஓதிப் பணிவது), an outward worship rare in these songs. The refrain plays on தெய்வ யானை: Ganapati, Airavata and Devayanai. The first lines (கல்விடாது ... மெய்கள் தோணி) are hard to divide.

1233.reading: The poet, infatuated by young women's poison carp eyes and breasts and by Kama's bodiless form, asks not to be born again into this world in the hut of suffering, and to be let worship at the feet that the devotees reach. The praise names Murugan the hero who embraced the hill girl, the vel that fought the eight mountains, the one who knows sweet Tamil set to music that the lord with matted hair praises, and the beautiful six-faced one with twelve eyes.
1233.nuance: இன்னிசை உறு தமிழ் தெரிவோனே: Murugan is the knower of Tamil with music, perhaps alluding to his teaching Siva, but the line (தன் நிறை சடை இறை என் முனி பரவரு) is unclear.

1234.reading: The poet asks for the threefold Tamil in Murugan's service, so that he may tell in parts the fame of the two feet that melting devotees beyond the gunas and faultless bhaktas strew with vetchi, and speak the name Murugan took as servant of the hill girl with coral lips and dark eyes. The praise names Krishna, who broke the tusks of the elephant Kamsa sent, and Siva who flayed the elephant and danced, and calls Murugan the one whose fierce vel calmed the three worlds, fought the asuras, churned the sea and freed the gods.
1234.nuance: த்ரயத் தமிழ், the three Tamils of prose, music and drama, is what the poet asks for. குறத்தி கிங்கரன் எனப் படைத்த பெயர் is Murugan's own title as Valli's servant. Whether பேசா means 'so as to speak' or 'not speaking' is unclear.

1235.reading: The poet describes a life of wife, servants, clan, pride and gathered wealth ending when the body falls like a broken pot, is wrapped in a small old rag and left at the burning ground, and asks to be given the red feet before the body is destroyed. The praise is a battle in drum syllables: trees fall roaring, the asuras' army flees, the mountains roar, the sage of four Vedas is made servant, the gods rise, and Indra of the thunderbolt is resettled in his world.
1235.nuance: சிறு பழைய துணி போர்த்தி: the rich man of the first lines is covered with a small old rag at the end, the reversal the song turns on. மறைநாலும் உடைய முனி ஆட்பட may be Brahma brought low, but he is not named. மொளமொளமொளாச் is drum syllable.

1236.reading: The poet asks that, before Death comes like a dark cloud, harrows him with his evil deeds and the sorrow of death draws near while he lies on darbha grass, he may stand with untroubled mind thinking of Murugan's feet, and that Murugan come on the peacock and give release. The praise calls Murugan the one who spoke a rare sweet word to the father who dances wearing arugu grass, moon, datura and river, who embraced the girl of a small clan in whom wisdom dawned, and who opened the asuras' prison while Brahma stood bewildered.
1236.nuance: தெர்ப்பை இடை: the dying man laid on darbha grass. மறலி ... துட்ட வினைகள் கொண்டு அலைத்து: Death torments with one's own deeds. சிறுகுலம் தனக்குள் அறிவு வந்து உதித்த சிறுமி praises Valli's wisdom, not only her beauty.

1237.reading: The poet describes women with lotus-bud breasts who call men to come, embrace them, take their money and then bite their lips again, and asks whether he must still suffer, drunk on the poison of desire. The praise calls Murugan the one who told a meaning to Siva of the crowned river and moon, the twelve-armed bridegroom of the hill girl, nephew of the emerald Vishnu lying on the serpent with the discus, and the one whose vel dried the sea.
1237.nuance: காசை அபகரித்து மீள இதழ் கடிப்பது: the theft of money comes between the embraces, which is the deceit. The word after மவுலியர்க்கு is unclear (சாவியது), but ஓர் அர்த்தம் மொழிவோனே gives Murugan telling Siva 'a meaning'.

1238.reading: The poet asks Murugan to clear away the pleasure of living proud of a sandal-adorned wife and children with anklets, called 'my wealth', so that sorrows fade, and to give his feet today. The praise calls Murugan the dweller of Kurinji with kadamba shoulders, the vel that split the hill, the beautiful one who dwells in the bodies of devotees who conquered the five senses, and the one who said 'fear not' when the worlds shook.
1238.nuance: எந்தன் தனங்கள் என்றென்று: wife and children are named as 'my wealth', so the plea is against possessiveness more than the household itself. ஐந்திந்த்ரியங்கள் வென்று ஒன்றும் அன்பர் அங்கம் பொருந்தும்: Murugan's dwelling is the body of the self-controlled devotee.

1239.reading: The poet asks whether his harsh karma will not end: in a body of water, filth, flesh, blood and bone, he does everything for maya, gathers elephants, children, wife, jewels, clothes and clan, rejoices in the womb's way, and studies arts, suffering daily without meaning. The praise calls Murugan the great life of the father who keeps the mountain's daughter at his side, the moon and river in his hair, axe and fire in his hand, the mountain as a bow, and who laughed down his foes, and the one who looks with grace on devotees in faultless tapas.
1239.nuance: கலைபல பிடித்து நித்தம் அலைபடும் அநர்த்தம்: learning is listed among the attachments, not set against them. மறைதொழ நகைத்த: Siva destroying his foes (Tripura) by a laugh, told in the text's own details.

1240.reading: The poet asks whether Murugan will not grant him, as those who know peace beyond have gained wisdom, a way to live in stillness with gaze half-closed, breath held, the light appearing, and Sivayoga stirring the soul, in the dance-form of the one who danced the dance of jnana and bliss while Uma sang. The praise pictures the hill of plantains like elephant trunks, mango honey and bees on vengai, and Murugan dwelling in the grove with the hill girl.
1240.nuance: தூங்கிய பார்வை ... தாங்கிய வாயு ... தோன்றிய சோதி ... சிவயோகம்: the plea is a compact list of yoga's stages, and சோம்பினில் வாழும் வகை, living in 'idleness', means the stillness of the yogi. Line 15 seems short of syllables.

1241.reading: The poet asks whether he must perish, not knowing how to drink the Siva-bliss of union with the lady of the lotus of Siva-knowledge, wandering as a form of impurity and panting after common women; he asks Murugan to come before him daily so he may play with the hosts of devotees and his impurities and twin deeds break. The praise names Uma, the bride, Gauri and Sivakami at Siva's side, who one day shared a pomegranate in the elephant's hand, and asks Murugan, her son, to grant the deathless abode of nectar to one born in vain.
1241.nuance: சிவஞான புண்டரிக மலர்மாது: Siva-knowledge is personified as a lady to be embraced, set against the common women (பொது மாதர்). The pomegranate shared by Uma is named but its story is not told.

1242.reading: The poet asks that the wretchedness of being cast off, after he served women of darting eyes and stopped giving the money they wanted, not harm him, and asks whether the light shining as bliss in the body and in the soul will not appear, the one spread out as six and eight that no one can describe. The praise is of the vel that split Sura's diamond chest and the golden hill, and of Murugan, hero of heroes, who saw the hunters' beautiful girl and joined her in love.
1242.nuance: காசைக் கொடாத பின்பு சீரற்று: when the money stops the man is ruined, the courtesan's logic. ஆறெட்டுமாய் விரிந்தும் may count the tattvas, but the number is unclear.

1243.reading: The poet, caught by women seeking wealth like a fish on the hook, asks that when Death comes by fate to seek his life he be given the thought to call 'Adi Muruga, Adi Muruga'. The praise calls Murugan the one who fought with the vel while the asuras cried out, the yoga peacock who bows at the feet of the guru of Om Namasivaya, Uma's son, nephew of Rama and Hari, dweller in devotees' hearts, and Devayanai's husband.
1243.nuance: ஆதிமுருகா ஆதிமுருகா ஆதிமுருகா என: the plea at the hour of death is simply for the name, repeated. ஓநமசிவாய குரு பாதம் makes Siva's mantra itself the guru at whose feet Murugan bows.

1244.reading: The poet, a ghoul for gold, land and women, a diseased doer of crores of sins, asks that when Death comes to drop him into the seven hells Murugan come fast on his steed, speaking the word of wisdom, so his sins go. The praise calls Murugan the vel that made the sea quake and Death fall and run, nephew of Krishna who climbed the kurundha tree with the women's saris, and the one who lives with the hill girl.
1244.nuance: செழுந்தாது பார் மாது: gold, earth and woman, the triple desire. விழுந்தோடவே காலன் in the praise answers the plea: Death himself falls. Several words are corrupt.

1245.reading: The poet asks to be given, before the failing time comes for wealth, servants, kin, sons and house, the thought of grace to melt in devotion and hold Murugan's feet daily. The praise names Rama who rolled the ten heads, calls Murugan the one whom the pot-bellied elephant god, eating cakes, puffed rice and honey, helped to embrace the hunter girl in the forest, and the one who told the Veda's word to the three-eyed lord who gives release.
1245.nuance: மொய்ப்பன் உதவ அடவிக்குள் மறமகளை அணைவோனே: Ganapati's help in the Valli story is named outright. முத்தி தரு முதல்வர் ... மறைமொழியை மொழிவோனே: Murugan teaching Siva, without naming Om.

1246.reading: The poet asks whether one should speak without end as the Puranas and Srutis, without seeking the one cause known by experience by those who rose saying 'enough' to pleasures, delusion, lust, fire-like anger, greed and the many forms of the sects. The praise tells of Murugan who, taking a form and feigning distress, judged the time and joined the hunter girl, armed with Kama's two arrows and bow, and whose vel resettled Indra and powdered the demon.
1246.nuance: அநுபூதி கொண்டு அறியும் ஒரு காரணம்: experience, not scripture or sect, knows the one cause. The question (விளம்புவதோதான்) may be the poet's self-rebuke or a jab at scholars; the sentence's subject is unclear.

links.note: Tirumular's dead man leaves the honey-haired woman, the wealth and the house and is carried to the common burning ground; 1235 lists wife, servants, clan and gathered wealth and ends with the body in a small old rag at the burning ground.

Tirumular's sectarians stay inside their sect and never gain the experience free of ego; 1246 asks whether one should speak endlessly as scripture instead of seeking the one cause known by experience (அநுபூதி), having said 'enough' to the sects.

source_issues: 1244: ஡ stands for ஊ in line 2 (யாதிலு஡மாசை, perhaps யாதிலும் ஊமாசை), and ஧வ்முழ்க in line 5 is corrupt for மூழ்க.
1240: line 15 (பூங்குற மாதினுட வாடியிருள்) is short of syllables.
1235, 1241: initial உ is split from its word by a space (உ டையமுனி, உ வகாரியன்பர்).
